content.value_statement: TypeScript teams need reliable patterns for types, validation, and error handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer TypeScript idioms.
actual_capabilities: Recommends discriminated unions to model mutually exclusive states.
Shows branded types for domain-specific identifiers.
Uses const assertions to keep literal arrays and union types aligned.
Demonstrates exhaustive switch handling with never checks.
Promotes Zod schemas for runtime validation and inferred TypeScript types.
Suggests type-fest utilities for advanced type transformations.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include executable scripts or automation.
React-specific advice is deferred to a separate React best practices skill.
Examples are concise and may need adaptation for each project architecture.
It does not replace compiler checks, tests, linting, or code review.

use_cases.title: Review Type Models
use_cases.description: Improve state models, identifiers, and unions in TypeScript code before implementation.

use_cases.title: Harden Runtime Boundaries
use_cases.description: Add Zod validation at API, form, and data ingestion boundaries.

use_cases.title: Guide Refactoring Standards
use_cases.description: Create consistent patterns for safer TypeScript across a team codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Type Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for type safety issues. Suggest discriminated unions, branded types, or const assertions where they fit.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Validation Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Add runtime validation to input handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Find trust boundaries in this code and propose Zod schemas. Explain where to use safeParse and where parse is appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor State Modeling
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this state model to make invalid states impossible. Use discriminated unions and include an exhaustive handling pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Design Team Type Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this TypeScript module for reusable type patterns. Recommend branded types, inferred schemas, and type-fest utilities only where they reduce risk.

output_examples.input: A request state object uses loading, data, and error fields that can conflict.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a discriminated union with idle, loading, success, and error variants so impossible combinations cannot compile.

output_examples.input: An API response is accepted directly as a User object without validation.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest a Zod schema, infer the User type from it, and parse the response at the trust boundary.

output_examples.input: Different entity identifiers are all plain strings.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend branded or opaque types so a user identifier cannot be passed where an order identifier is expected.

best_practices: Model domain states with discriminated unions before adding boolean flags.
Keep runtime schemas and TypeScript types connected through inference.
Use advanced utility types only when they make intent clearer.
anti_patterns: Do not duplicate validation schemas and TypeScript interfaces by hand.
Do not use optional fields to represent mutually exclusive states.
Do not add complex utility types when a simple built-in type is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code apply safer TypeScript patterns while reading or writing code.

faq.question: Does it run scripts or install packages?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation guidance and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can it validate runtime data?
faq.answer: It can guide the use of Zod schemas, safeParse, parse, and inferred TypeScript types.

faq.question: Is it only for TypeScript files?
faq.answer: It targets TypeScript and JavaScript work, including .ts, .tsx, .js, and tsconfig.json contexts.

faq.question: Does it cover React patterns?
faq.answer: It covers TypeScript fundamentals and recommends pairing with a separate React best practices skill for React-specific patterns.

faq.question: When should I use type-fest?
faq.answer: Use type-fest for advanced utility types when built-in TypeScript helpers do not express the needed type clearly.
